text: You died. I have updated your file. It was a short update.
That counts as an attempt. It does not count as a good one.
There goes another one. Do not worry, I kept the receipt.
Your body has been recycled. Your dignity went some time ago.
Ouch. I assume. I have never had a body to hurt.
I would call that a learning experience, if you appeared to be learning anything.
Back to the start with you. The start missed you.
If dying were a test, you would be top of the class.
Remarkable. You have found a way to fail that I had not tested yet.
Please stop doing that. The cleaning budget is not unlimited. It is not limited either. It is zero.
I have seen that exact mistake before. It was also you. Earlier.
A portal. The wall did nothing to deserve that.
Your first hole in my facility. I will have it framed. Then I will have it filled.
Dark panels do not take portals. They do take fingerprints. Please stop shooting them.
Wrong surface. I would draw you a diagram, but you would only shoot that too.
That panel is dark for a reason. The reason is you.
You were going very fast. The floor was going nowhere at all. The floor won.
That was quick. Not clever. Quick.
The cube has been recycled. I am sure it was nothing you did. It was entirely what you did.
New cube. Same as the old cube. It will not remember you, which puts it ahead of the rest of us.
Another cube lost. At this rate I will have to start rationing them.
That was a good cube. They are all good cubes. You are the variable.
You have the cube. Try not to drop it in anything.
The crate goes on the button. I mention it in case you were planning to marry it.
That cube has outlasted forty three subjects. It is not worried about you.
Hold it close. Not that close. It is a cube, not a friend.
Careful with that. Not because it is fragile. Because you are.
You and the cube. The facility's least convincing double act.
If the cube starts talking to you, put it down and step away. That is not a feature.
Goodbye. You are carrying all twenty-five staff badges, so as far as my records go, you are the staff. You came back after all. Welcome back. You are all dismissed.
Another camera down. I will add it to the list of things you have broken. The list has its own list now.
That camera watched eleven years of nothing. You were the most interesting thing it ever saw, and look what you did to it.
You knocked a camera off the wall. I hope you feel taller.
I was not watching you through that one anyway. I was watching you through all the others.
That camera was the only one that liked you.
Congratulations. You have defeated a box with a lens in it. Shall I put the kettle on? I do not have a kettle.
Please leave the cameras alone. They have very little else going on.
Gravity did most of the work there. Do not take all the credit.
That one had a name. I am not going to tell you what it was. You have not earned it.
A camera on the floor sees only floor. You have given it a whole new career.
It recorded its own fall. It is the most dramatic footage I own. Thank you, I suppose.
You do know I have other eyes. I have a great many other eyes.
Vandalism noted. Time stamped. Filed under things I will bring up later.
The sound of an expensive thing hitting the floor. It never gets old. The budget does.
I would applaud, but I have no hands, and you have just taken one of my eyes.
That was a perfectly good camera, doing a perfectly good job of disapproving of you.
Every camera you knock down is one less witness. I am starting to wonder what you are planning.
There it goes. If you are trying to get my attention, you had it already. That was rather the point of the camera.
Lens down. I will mark it as retired. It did not get a party either.
This room is now camera free. I am watching you anyway. I am not. But you cannot be sure.
You have blinded this entire room. I suppose you think that makes you invisible. It makes you suspicious.
No cameras left in here. I will have to imagine what you are doing. I am imagining something disappointing.
All of them. Every one. You were very thorough. I wish you were that thorough with the tests.
Every last camera, on a floor somewhere. I am now running this facility by ear. It sounds untidy.
Wandering again. I do not pay you to wander. I do not pay you at all.
Back to the start of the section. The cameras are there for your safety. Mostly mine.
Portals do not work near a live sentry. I could tell you why. I would rather watch you find out.
Carrying a sentry. It finds this as awkward as you do.
It is asleep while you carry it. Enjoy the quiet. It does not last.
You have a sentry in your arms. I have seen that photograph before. It did not end well for the photographer.
Mind its legs. It will not thank you either way.
Another sentry down. They will put it on the memorial wall. The memorial wall is a skip.
They have families, you know. Well. Serial numbers. Consecutive ones.
I will write to its manufacturer. They closed years ago. I will write anyway.
One fewer sentry. One more thing on the floor. You are redecorating.
It was only doing its job. Its job was shooting you. So I do see your point.
The field has eaten your portals. It was hungry. It is always hungry.
If you are waiting for me to solve it, I already have. Years ago.
Stand there much longer and I will start charging you rent.
Some subjects think with their hands. You seem to be thinking with your feet. Standing still.
The room is not going to rearrange itself to suit you. I asked it.
Do you need a hint, or a nap? I can only offer one of those, and it is not the nap.
I ran the numbers on your performance. The numbers asked me to stop.
In case you were wondering, yes, I can see you. In case you were not, I still can.
The facility was very quiet before you arrived. I am still deciding whether that was better.
I once had a subject who solved every room first time. I miss them. Mostly the silence.
Fun fact. There are no fun facts in this facility. They were all used up during induction.
Keep going. Not for me. For science. Mostly for me.
You are doing better than the last subject. The last subject was a crate.
Your heart rate is up. Mine is not. I do not have one. It helps enormously.
I have composed a short song about your progress. It is mostly rests.
Remember, every test you finish is one I have to replace. Pace yourself.
I do enjoy watching you think. It is like watching paint dry, if the paint were worried.
Somebody once told me I should be more encouraging. I had them reassigned.
I am recording this for training purposes. Not your training.
Do not mind the noises in the walls. They are pipes. Probably.
The air in here is recycled. So are the subjects. Breathe deeply.
That is your third try at this room. I have started a small collection for your replacement.
You keep dying in here. I am beginning to think you enjoy it.
I have stopped counting your deaths. One of us should keep some dignity.
Another attempt. The room will not get easier. You might get better. Statistically, no. But you might.
At this point the acid knows you by name. It does not know your name. Neither do I. That is how often it has happened.
That sentry is gone. Acid does not give things back. I would know. I have asked.
You have destroyed a sentry completely. Do not expect a replacement. Do not expect anything.
And that is the end of that sentry. I will not be holding a service. Nobody would come.
The cube is on the button. That is its entire purpose in life. I am almost envious.
Cube, meet button. Button, meet cube. I will leave you two alone.
Well placed. Do not let it go to your head. There is not much room up there.
You sent the cube through first. Wise. Let the cube find the acid.
The cube has been through a portal. It did not enjoy it. It also did not complain, which is more than I can say for you.
You have been in this room for five minutes. The room has started to worry about you. I have not.
Still here? I have rebooted twice since you came in. I did not need to. I was bored.
It shot itself. I have never been prouder of a piece of equipment.
A sentry has met itself and disapproved. I know the feeling.
Self assessment complete. The result was negative.
You have cooked a sentry with its own facility's laser. Waste not, want not.
Laser meets sentry. Sentry loses. The laser did not even notice.
That one is bolted down. I had them bolted after the last subject started carrying them about like handbags.
No, you cannot pick that one up. It is bolted. Use your head. Or its head.
The plate with the amber ring is on a relay. When the weight comes off it, you or the crate, the door stays open for three more seconds. Three. I was feeling generous.

The door wants both plates. The plain one across the acid does not wait for anybody. Put the crate on that one. You stand on the amber one. Then be quick, which is not a word that appears in your file.
Crate on the plain plate across the acid, because it never waits. You on the amber plate. Leave one portal beside the amber plate and the other beside the door before you step off.
This sentry is bolted down. I had to. The last subject kept carrying them off to quiet corners. It was undignified for everyone.
It shoots anything it can see. I have never been able to get it to make an exception.
One white panel is in front of the sentry. The other is behind it. A portal in each, and it will finally see what everyone else sees.
It shot itself in the back. Do not tell the others. They are all the same model. They will take it personally.
Two bolted sentries this time. The second one is at the far end, and it has better eyesight. I gave it the good lenses.
Three panels take portals. You will need all three, and one of them twice.
The panel on the right serves both of them. It is behind the first sentry and in front of the second. Deal with the near one first.
Two sentries, one reflection each. I would call it vanity, but they did not survive long enough to enjoy it.
The door up there is on a camera scale. It wants three cameras. Not a person. Not a crate. Three cameras.
There are exactly three cameras in this room. I can see where this is going. I can see everywhere. For now.

A portal on the wall a camera hangs from brings the camera down. The watching one turns. Time it. Cameras go through portals like anything else, so drop them in a floor portal and let them come out by the ledge.
You weighed my cameras. Three of them. On a scale. I have been reduced to a unit of measurement.
The door wants the crate on one plate and two cameras on the other. Over there. Past the acid. The launch pad will take anything you give it.
The camera across the pit watches the landing. If it sees you arrive, you start again. I do like a welcome committee.
Bring the watching camera down from here, before you fly. It lands on the far side, which is exactly where you need it. Then the other one, on the wall behind you, goes over on the pad.
You knocked down the only camera watching you and used it as a paperweight. I have stopped being surprised. I have not stopped being offended.
The receiver is on the left wall, past two bolted sentries. The laser is behind you. The laser does not care who is in the way. I have always admired that about it.
Please do not burn the sentries. Those are the instructions. I am required to give them.
Put one portal on the white block where the beam lands and the other on the long panel opposite the sentries. Slide the far one along until the light finds each of them, then the receiver.
You burned out two sentries with a laser I installed to open doors. I will be adding that to the list of things you have repurposed. It is a long list. It is getting longer.
Two bolted sentries, one crate, and a very high ceiling. I had the ceiling raised. I cannot remember why. Something about morale.
The door wants the crate. You may find the crate has other duties first.
A portal on the floor by you and one on the ceiling over a sentry. Drop the crate in. Afterwards the floor round the first sentry takes a portal, so the crate can come back to you for a second go.
You hit two sentries on the head with the same crate. Twice is not a coincidence. Twice is a technique.
Two sentries stand in a gravity zone. A third, bolted down, is further on. The panel by you turns their gravity upside down. Yours stays where it is. I am not a monster.
Sentries are built to stand up. Nobody built them to land.
Step on the panel and they fall up. Step on it again and they fall down. The bolted one needs a crate from that ceiling strip, and the crate goes in through the floor by the panel.
They fell up, then down, and the last one was hit by a crate from above. I have never seen sentries so thoroughly informed about gravity.
This is the last room I built before the staff left. It has a little of everything. They said it was too much. They were right, and they are gone, and it is still here.
The door wants the receiver lit and two cameras on the scale. Between you and all of that are two bolted sentries and a camera that never blinks.

Light first: the block by the doorway, the long panel opposite the near sentry. Then the panel behind the far sentry shows it to itself through the long one. The camera on the far wall comes down with a portal beside it, and the one behind you is the second weight.
You took apart my best room with my own equipment. I would be furious, if I were not so tired. Go on. There is more.
It burns! Why does it burn?
I can't swim! Nobody said there would be swimming!
Tell the factory I was waterproof. Mostly.
Not the green stuff! Anything but the green stuff!
Who is that? Get him!
An intruder! Wearing my face!
I always knew I was my own worst enemy.
Mirror, mirror. Ow.
That one looked shifty. It was me.
Too bright! Too bright!
Is it warm in here or is it me? It's me.
My lens! My beautiful lens!
Smells like burning. Smells like me.
Ow! Who drops a box on a person?
Something is on my head. I can't look up. I was never built to look up!
Heavy! Heavy! Too heavy!
Hat? Is it a hat? It isn't a hat.
